content: User-facing fabro validate messages must be built as single-line format! strings (multi-line only via backslash-newline continuations verified by compilation), and the rule test must assert the EXACT expected message text, not substring containment. Substring assertions let mangled literals (embedded whitespace runs from scripted edits) pass review and ship garbled CLI output.

description: Cross-language string editing silently mangles Rust line continuations
resolution: Fixed in the fabro-900e review round: rewrote the two diagnostics in context_append_keys_within_allow.rs with real backslash-newline continuations and exact-equality assertions in the rule test (commit dc5959a80).

title: Per-node tool policy: allow-only explicit lists — no presets, no deny, no run-level list
rationale: Decided 2026-08-27 grilling for fabro-47b5 (ADR-0009 amendment). One attribute tools=<canonical names>, unset = default open. Presets are a blackbox in the graph and leak-free explicit lists self-document; deny lists cannot express read-only safely (MCP tools are run-config-dependent, future native tools leak); a run-level allowlist reintroduces replace-vs-narrow two-layer ambiguity. Presets may return later if lists grow unwieldy.

name: PermissionLevel origin: upstream interactive CLI approval axis
description: PermissionLevel (ReadOnly/ReadWrite/Full) was introduced upstream 2026-02-23 (Bryan Helmkamp, agent CLI approval callback). Enforced ONLY in the interactive CLI path via is_auto_approved(level, tool_category) at fabro-agent cli.rs ~153 (--permissions flag, default ReadWrite). Wire-contracted in OpenAPI (run events + projection). Workflow sessions report Full truthfully (no approval gating) and must never derive or remove it; tool restriction is a separate axis projected via agent_tools.
